flags: Kansas Tourism 00 prints K-177 and exit 135; local tourism 01 gives Highway 147 and exit 134. Reservoir 08 independently places K-147 across the dam. Used K-147 and omitted exit numbers.
Bluff height differs: tourism 01 and park 02 say 100 feet; reservoir 08 says 150 feet. Omitted height rather than silently select one. Current height claim is therefore withheld.

Attack chronology differs: 02 says the 1850s, while 01 and 08 say 1867. No tribal or primary history corroborates participants, deaths, destination or burning. Retained the landmark moment, but omitted current’s attack, Salt Lake City destination and burned-machine narrative pending better evidence.
Tourism 01 says the reservoir was created in 1949; 08 gives construction from 1949 to 1951. Story distinguishes construction start from completion.
No construction or designation history of the modern scenic route is cached. The overview instead distinguishes the modern byway from the older trail it crosses.

Current’s claim that the canyon already bore names when church stone was quarried is only broadly supported by mid-19th-century carvings and 1902 construction; the new text reports those facts separately. No current moment coordinates were supplied, so none were added.
